title: The Garden of Caerlum
premise: Quentin Joubert, a runaway apprentice hiding a modest gift in the magic-outlawed city of Caerlum, discovers their hedge-witch mentor bound an ancient power into them at birth: the last living vessel of the Verdant Crown, the artifact that once ended—and could reignite—the war between mages and mortals. When the crown's witch-hunters begin testing every citizen's blood, Quentin is forced to flee with a disgraced hunter, Sera Vane, who has her own reasons to doubt the throne. As the long winter closes in, Quentin must choose between destroying the Crown within them (and their own life), surrendering it to a scheming royal spymaster, or awakening it and becoming the tyrant everyone fears. In the end, Quentin splits the Crown's power into the land itself—dying briefly, returning changed, no longer human alone but part of Caerlum's soil—so that magic belongs to no one and everyone.
about_author: F. M. Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval herbals before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about inheritance, small magics, and the people history forgets to record.

chapters.title: Charms for Copper
chapters.summary: Third-person limited on Quentin, selling luck-knots and fever-charms in Caerlum's night market while hiding their gift behind sleight of hand. A child customer's charm works too well, drawing attention. Emotional beat: the exhausting loneliness of a life built on concealment.

chapters.title: The Proclamation
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Royal criers announce the Gift-Hunt: mandatory blood-testing at the parish wells by month's end. Quentin watches neighbors who once bought charms now denounce magic loudest. Beat: fear curdling into betrayal as the city turns on its own quiet histories.

chapters.title: What Marisol Left Me
chapters.summary: Quentin returns to their buried past, opening the hidden box their mentor Marisol left twelve years ago, never dared opened. Inside: a living seed of green light that answers Quentin's pulse. Beat: dread and wonder—the discovery that their invisibility was always someone else's design.

chapters.title: The Hunter at the Door
chapters.summary: Sera Vane, a Gift-Hunter with a reputation for mercy, tests Quentin's boarding house and hesitates over Quentin's blood vial. POV shifts to Sera, revealing she falsifies results for those who remind her of her executed sister. Beat: two liars recognizing each other.

chapters.title: Ash Wednesday Market
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. The night market is raided; Quentin's friend Odile the charm-seller is taken, and Quentin's suppressed power flares involuntarily, healing a trampled boy in full view. Beat: guilt and panic—the moment hiding stops being possible.

chapters.title: Flight Along the Wall
chapters.summary: Sera finds Quentin before the other hunters do and offers escape in exchange for answers about the green seed. They flee over Caerlum's frozen aqueduct. Beat: reluctant alliance, trust extended like a loan neither expects repaid.

chapters.title: The Spymaster's Garden
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Lord Cassel, the royal spymaster, reveals he knows what Quentin carries: he has hunted the Verdant Crown for twenty years and offers Sera her sister's restored name in exchange for delivering it. Beat: temptation dressed as justice.

chapters.title: Hollow Chapel
chapters.summary: Quentin and Sera shelter in a ruined chapel where Marisol once trained; Quentin reads her carved warnings and learns the Crown was split from a dying goddess to end the Mage War. Beat: grief for Marisol reframed as understanding—she wasn't hiding Quentin, she was protecting the world.

chapters.title: Blood in the Snow
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Bounty hunters ambush them; Quentin's power erupts, killing a man for the first time. Sera sees the scale of what Quentin carries. Beat: horror at oneself, and Sera's choice to stay anyway.

chapters.title: The Village That Remembers
chapters.summary: They reach Thornhollow, a village quietly practicing old rites, led by elder Bramwen who recognizes the seed. She explains the three paths: destroy it, wield it, or return it to the land. Beat: belonging offered for the first time—and the weight of choice made communal.

chapters.title: Sera's Confession
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. She admits she reported her sister years ago under coercion, and that Cassel owns her. Quentin must decide whether to trust her still. Beat: forgiveness as a deliberate act, not a feeling.

chapters.title: Cassel's Summons
chapters.summary: Cassel's riders surround Thornhollow; he offers Quentin sanctuary, research, and control—if Quentin surrenders the Crown alive. He shows proof Marisol died in his custody. Beat: rage and the seductive promise that power could be used well, this time, by me.

chapters.title: The Long Winter Falls
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Snow seals the passes; the village starves while Quentin secretly draws on the seed to keep greenhouses alive, weakening themselves. Beat: the corruption theme embodied—every mercy paid for with a piece of self.

chapters.title: Bramwen's Price
chapters.summary: Bramwen reveals the rite of Returning requires a willing death, and that she performed it once before and failed. Quentin's POV. Beat: terror metabolized into resolve; Quentin begins preparing to die.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Well
chapters.summary: A Thornhollow youth, terrified for his family, sells their location to Cassel. Riders burn the greenhouses. Sera is captured covering Quentin's escape. Beat: despair, and Quentin's first taste of how power isolates even among friends.

chapters.title: The Throne Room of Roots
chapters.summary: Quentin walks willingly into Cassel's citadel to trade themselves for Sera and the village prisoners. Cassel's ritual to extract the Crown begins. Beat: sacrifice chosen freely, the story's moral center.

chapters.title: What the Crown Shows You
chapters.summary: Inside the extraction, Quentin experiences the Crown's memory: the goddess's death, the war, every hand that grasped it and rotted. Cassel, linked to the rite, sees it too and wavers. Beat: climax of the corruption theme—power showing its true face to its would-be owner.

chapters.title: Vane's Choice
chapters.summary: Sera breaks free during the chaos, and instead of fleeing, chooses to hold the ritual circle open so Quentin can complete the Returning. Beat: redemption earned through action; her sister's name spoken aloud as defiance.

chapters.title: The Returning
chapters.summary: Climax. Quentin pours the Crown into Caerlum's soil through the citadel's foundations, dying as green fire spreads through the frozen land. Cassel, refusing to let go, is unmade by the power he tried to seize. Beat: awe and loss—the cost fully paid.

chapters.title: Spring Out of Season
chapters.summary: Quentin wakes in Thornhollow days later, changed: they hear the land's slow voice, feel seasons in their bones, no longer wholly human but no longer hunted. Magic stirs gently in ordinary people. Beat: rebirth without triumphalism.

chapters.title: The Reckoning of Names
chapters.summary: Sera dismantles the Hunt from inside, testifying against Cassel's network; Odile and the taken charm-sellers are freed. Quentin refuses a role as prophet or queen, insisting the gift belongs to everyone. Beat: justice as repair, not vengeance.

chapters.title: The Garden of Caerlum
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Quentin's POV. Spring comes early to a scarred city; Quentin plants Marisol's herb garden on the chapel ruins, teaching children charms openly. Final beat: identity resolved—not the vessel of a dead power, but a gardener of a living one.
